meaning: The thing one stage of the loop hands to the next, such as a decoded frame, a simulation step, a training sample or an action, counted per second to compare machines.
A computer that sits beside the robot, where power is the scarce resource and nothing is billed by the hour.
A small program run in place of a real workload, loading a machine the way that workload does without being it.
Units of work per second divided by watts drawn under load: how much work a machine does with a fixed amount of energy.
How an instance hour is bought: on demand, as Spot capacity that AWS can take back, or reserved ahead; each has its own price.
The AWS location an instance runs in; prices differ between Regions.
Spare EC2 capacity that AWS may take back; for a batch on Spot, count only the units that finished, since a unit lost when the machine is reclaimed delivers nothing.
One GPU running for one hour.
A program launched on the GPU; nvidia-smi's utilisation counts the time at least one is running, not how much of the GPU it uses.
The time between two commands to the motors: 33.3 ms when the arm is driven at 30 Hz. A policy call's deadline is counted in control periods.
Several future actions returned by one policy call, played one per control period while the next call computes.
Starting the next policy call while the current chunk is still playing, so the arm does not stop to wait.
The time within which half of all calls finish; it describes the typical call.
The time within which ninety-nine calls in every hundred finish; held against the room a chunk leaves when one late call in a hundred is tolerable.
The resource that fills while the rest of the machine sits partly idle; a workload is priced on the instance built around that part. For the policy stand-in it is memory bandwidth.
EC2 GPU instances whose GPUs also carry graphics and video hardware, including RT cores.
EC2 GPU instances built for training; their GPUs lack RT cores, and the H100 in P5 does not decode AV1.
GPU units that trace rays, which a ray-traced camera renderer needs.
The video compression LeRobot records in by default; decoding it needs a decoder that supports it, or CPU cores.
A robot physics simulator; two releases (4.0.1 and 3.17.0) ran our physics and render stand-ins.
NVIDIA's inference compiler, the runtime behind its 149.0 ms Jetson Orin median for GR00T N1.7.
The Jetson's own command-line monitor of power and load; its VDD_IN rail covers the whole board.
NVIDIA's command-line tool that reports GPU status, including utilisation and GPU power.
AWS's own Arm processors, offered as EC2 CPU instances.
The interface MuJoCo's offscreen renderer used for hardware-accelerated drawing without a display; our render run did not establish how much of each frame the GPU drew.
One call in a hundred is slower than the p99, so holding the p99 against the room a chunk leaves accepts one late call in a hundred; accepting none means holding the worst call.
A board's purchase price divided by the units per second it sustains: what each unit per second of capacity cost to buy.
The three conditions under which a ratio of two rates belongs to the two machines: the same unit, the same model and the same software release.
